description: At the 2026-06-17 FOMC — Kevin Warsh's first meeting as Fed Chair — the Committee held the target range at 3.50-3.75% (unanimous 12-0) but flipped its forward guidance HAWKISH: the median dot for end-2026 rose to 3.8% (from 3.4% in March), REMOVING the prior outlook for a 2026 cut and signaling at least one HIKE is now seen as likely. Post-meeting, traders began pricing a hike as early as October. The statement attributes elevated inflation in part to supply shocks driving energy prices (the Iran/Hormuz conflict) and notes solid growth, strong capex/productivity, and a labor market keeping pace (the strong May jobs print). This is a regime shift from the disinflation-cut path the market had assumed: long-duration/rate-sensitive equities (grid/utilities, solar, real estate) face a higher-for-longer discount-rate headwind, the USD/DXY is supported, and gold faces a higher-real-rate headwind partly offset by its stagflation/energy-shock hedge bid.
user_notes: Registered 2026-06-29 in the scan refresh. The hawkish dot-plot flip is the single biggest macro regime change since the last review (2026-06-12): the Fed went from a hold-with-a-cut-bias to a hold-with-a-HIKE-bias, with an Oct hike now in play. Cross-cutting macro catalyst (not tied to one structural). Transmission: (1) HEADWIND to long-duration/rate-sensitive books we hold conviction in — grid_infrastructure (mov_20260604 grid position), solar, real_estate; risk_discipline rate-stops on those movements should be re-read. (2) USD support — a yfinance-priced EURUSD invalidation stop on the copper movement (inv_04) is rate-linked. (3) Gold: net-ambiguous (real-rate headwind vs energy-shock/stagflation hedge), consistent with gold's pullback to ~$4,187 from its ATH. Linked to the Hormuz energy shock (the inflation source the Fed is reacting to) and to the 06-05 selloff (which already had a yields/jobs leg). is_priced_in 0.5: yields moved on the day; the actual Oct-hike decision is unresolved.
